title: Serving GLM-5.3 at 607.8 tok/s across two Nvidia DGX stations with vLLM
lede: An NVIDIA tutorial serves the 753-billion-parameter GLM-5.3 NVFP4 model from two linked DGX Stations with vLLM, because its weights no longer fit in a single GB300's memory.

points: The quantized MoE checkpoint is about 464 GB, against 252 GB of HBM3e on one GB300, and activates 40 billion parameters per token.
The two machines link over ConnectX-8 RDMA and split the weights with tensor parallelism (TP=2) behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
The vLLM launch turns on multi-token prediction drafting four tokens per step, an FP8 KV cache and prefix caching.
Throughput peaks at 607.8 tokens per second at concurrency 16, then falls to 385.0 at 32, where mean request latency reaches 453.5 seconds.

points.text: Commenters run the cost maths: at about $100k per Station, one estimate puts payback near seven years against API prices, so the case rests on privacy or compliance.
One commenter says eight Blackwell workstation cards serve the model for about half the price with more throughput; a reply notes the Station's point is that it is a desktop.
Readers clarify the headline figure is aggregate across 16 users, a bit over 35 tok/s each, while a single user sees about 107.
Others warn that roughly 1.6 kW per machine, with matching fan noise, makes this a poor fit for homes or small businesses.
